messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert: Increased tail latency and sporadic 503s on /v1/embeddings in hosted/eu-central-1 since 09:12 UTC. Error rate ~0.8% but p99 token latency > 4s. Oncall paging: Mira (rotation).

Mira (oncall): I'm live. grabbing traces and rolling logs now. tagging eng-sre and runtime. will update in 8m.

Sam (eng-sre): thanks. I'm watching infra metrics. any tenant-specific signal?

Mira (oncall): initial sampling shows elevated queue depth on inference workers serving long-context jobs; a few workers reporting GPU OOMs and container restarts.

Kai (eng-runtime): we just pushed a new memory allocator tweak in canary this morning. could be correlated. rolling back canary cluster would be quickest test.

Mira (oncall): coordinate canary rollback for canary-set-3. Sam, can you handle rollback and temp capacity increase? I'll hold on pushing broader changes until we see results.

Sam (eng-sre): doing: `kubectl set image deploy/infra-canary allocator=allocator:v2.0.1 -n eu-central-1` to revert to v2.0.0. also increasing nodegroup buffer +2 instances. posting logs in 4m.

Devon (customer-success): FYI AcmeBank and BetaRetail pinged support about "slow embeddings" a few minutes ago. want to send a heads-up?

Tess (product-ops): draft for status page: "Investigating degraded embedding latency in eu-central-1 impacting a subset of customers. Mitigation in progress." keep short.

Mira (oncall): add "possible intermittent 503s; no data loss" to status. Sam, please confirm when canary rollback finished.

Sam (eng-sre): rollback applied at 09:20 UTC on canary-set-3. monitoring. immediate drop in restart rate on those pods. p99 on canaries down from 4.8s to 1.0s.

Kai (eng-runtime): that's a strong indicator. the allocator change unexpectedly increased transient memory usage for long contexts. we should not rollout further until RCA.

StatusBot: Status update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1987 3: "Investigating: degraded embedding latency in eu-central-1"

Mira (oncall): can we do staged rollback across remaining pools? want to avoid autoscaler thrash. Sam, please proceed with sequential rollback with cooldowns.

Sam (eng-sre): rolling through remaining pools with 3m cooldowns. using `--grace-period` to avoid immediate terminations. will keep node buffer +1. ETA for full rollback ~18m.

Devon (customer-success): I'll send a short note to affected customers now: "We're aware of elevated inference latency and intermittent errors in eu-central-1. We're rolling mitigations and will update when service is restored." send?

Mira (oncall): go ahead. keep it concise and offer a follow-up RCA.

Devon (customer-success): sent at 09:27 UTC to impacted tenants. included link to status page and contact details.

Kai (eng-runtime): after rollback progresses, I'm going to add a canary gate to allocator feature flags and add a perf test for long-context sequences that had failed previously. also adding detailed allocator metrics (peak transient allocs).

Sam (eng-sre): full rollback complete at 09:35 UTC. region p99 stabilized to 0.9-1.3s by 09:40 UTC. observed ~70% reduction in pod restarts.

Mira (oncall): marking as mitigated. updating status: "Mitigated: rollback applied; performance returning to normal. No data loss reported."

StatusBot: Status update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1987 3: "Mitigated: rollback applied; performance returning to normal."

Devon (customer-success): sent customer follow-up at 09:43 UTC announcing mitigation and promise of RCA.

Tess (product-ops): drafting customer-facing RCA template. here's a proposed text (please tweak):

```
Hello <Customer>,

Summary: On <date> between 09:12 and 09:40 UTC, a subset of customers in our eu-central-1 region experienced elevated embedding latency and intermittent 503 errors. Root cause: a recent change to the memory allocator (allocator v2.0.1) introduced transient peak allocations with long-context embedding workloads, causing OOMs and container restarts on a portion of the fleet.

What we did: We identified the canary signal and rolled back the allocator change across affected pools by 09:35 UTC. Normal service resumed by 09:40 UTC. There was no request data loss or exposure.

Preventative actions:
- Add canary gating for allocator changes and increase canary sample size for long-context traffic.
- Add a targeted CI perf test for long-context embedding requests.
- Instrument allocator-level metrics and set alert thresholds for transient peak allocs.
- Update deployment runbook: when OOM-related restarts spike during rollouts, initiate immediate rollback and scale buffer.

If you'd like a tenant-specific log extract or a call to discuss impact, please let us know and we'll schedule time.

Thanks,
Redwood Inference Support
```

Mira (oncall): couple of timeline clarifications for the RCA: deploy of allocator v2.0.1 at 08:50 UTC to canary; expanded rollout started 09:05; first anomalies 09:12; pager 09:14; canary rollback 09:20; full rollback done 09:35; mitigation observed 09:40. include these exact times.

Kai (eng-runtime): also include technical note: allocator introduced a faster-path allocation for small buffers but used a shared pool that for long-context sequences caused fragmentation and occasional transient peaks. long-context workload = sequence lengths > 32k tokens.

Sam (eng-sre): ops follow-ups: INF-2099 3 "Allocator rollout guard + perf test" assigned, ETA 72h. INF-2100 3 "Add allocator metrics + OOM alarm" assigned, ETA 48h.

Devon (customer-success): scheduling personalized follow-ups to top impacted customers tomorrow. will include tenant-specific timelines if requested.

Tess (product-ops): let's also prepare an internal comms snippet for execs: short summary, impact window, mitigation, next steps. I'll draft and circulate.

Mira (oncall): final note for rotation: when paging for latency with OOM pattern, escalate to runtime immediately and consider immediate canary rollback if canary shows improvement. added to runbook. closing thread and moving RCA to postmortems channel. :white_check_mark:
